So the plus is an item to collect, and the goal is probably to bring the block to the top box (exit) after collecting the plus.
Also, the yellow bar shrank further (currently at cols ~18-54).
So: collected the plus (item). Next, head to the top box: from (30,19): UP (25,19), LEFT? No, that's wrong. Path: (25,19) → RIGHT? Wait, I need to go to (25,34), then up the neck:
(30,19) --UP--> (25,19) --RIGHT--> (25,24) --RIGHT--> (25,29) --RIGHT--> (25,34) --UP--> (20,34) --UP--> (15,34) --UP--> (10,34).
7 moves. Then the block will be at rows 10-14, cols 34-38, inside the pillar, directly beneath the box (the box is at rows 9-15, cols 33-39). The block might need to enter the box: the box is a black 7x7. The block at (10,34) overlaps with the box's area (rows 10-14 ⊂ 9-15, cols 34-38 ⊂ 33-39). If the box is a solid obstacle, the move to (10,34) might be blocked... but (10,34) is within the pillar's range (rows 8-16, cols 32-40), and the box occupies rows 9-15, cols 33-39 within that. Hmm, is the box drawn on top of the pillar? The pillar is rows 8-16, cols 32-40 (gray), and the box (black) is rows 9-15, cols 33-39, drawn on top of it. So visually, the box covers the pillar. If the block moves to (10,34), it would overlap with the box's pixels.
Maybe the box is the goal zone: the block enters → level complete. Or the box is a solid obstacle and the goal is (15,34) (rows 15-19: rows 15-16 are the pillar below the box, rows 17-19 are the neck).
Anyway, let's try: execute the 7 moves and see what happens. If the last move is blocked, the block will stop at (15,34).
Actually, to be safe, let's do it in stages: first UP, RIGHT, RIGHT, RIGHT, UP (5 moves) → (20,34). Then UP, UP, UP (3 moves) → (10,34). Check after each stage. No, let's just batch all 7 and check the result; even if the last one is blocked, no harm done (it just won't move, and the bar will decrease by 1).
